ALL THREE CLAUSES VERIFIED BY THE CLOSER against real bd 1.1.2 and real br 0.2.19, in scratch workspaces, with target/debug/pact.

CLAUSE 1 - 'locates br and prefers it over bd when both are present, falling back to bd otherwise'. MET, WITH ONE DELIBERATE NARROWING that is recorded here because the code, not this bead text, is now the truth. Shipped rule: an existing .beads/ store PINS the backend (embeddeddolt/ -> bd, *.db -> br, both -> bd); br is preferred only when there is no store yet. Verified both directions:
  br init workspace:  pact whoami --json -> "bd_binary":"br", "bd_version":"br 0.2.19", "problems":[]
  bd init workspace:  pact whoami --json -> "bd_binary":"bd", "bd_version":"bd version 1.1.2 (20e493e56)"
  this repo (BOTH stores on disk after a stray br init, both binaries on PATH): pact whoami -> bd
Unconditional 'prefer br' would have been a data-loss-shaped bug: the backends do not share a store, so on any machine with both installed every existing bd repo would have opened an empty SQLite database and reported an empty inbox. The bead's wording is the thing that was wrong; nobody should 'fix' the code to match it.

CLAUSE 2 - every flag msg.rs relies on has a br equivalent discovered empirically. Re-run by me against br 0.2.19, not taken on trust:
  br create --type=message --title= --description= --assignee= --actor= --json
    -> {"id":"...","issue_type":"message","assignee":"bravo","created_by":"alpha",...}  WORKS, same argv as bd
  --parent, label add <ids...> <label>  WORKS, byte-identical argv to bd, idempotent -> the read-by-<agent> read-state mechanism needed zero code change
  --no-inherit-labels -> 'error: unexpected argument' — GAP, and correctly handled by omission rather than emulation: a br child is born with no labels, so the bug the flag prevents cannot occur there

Dual-era now. The era is decided per REQUEST (modern _meta selects modern, initialize selects legacy, and initialize is matched before _meta is consulted) because the modern revisions have no session for a connection-wide answer to live in — which is the spec's own rule for a dual-era server.

server/discover returns supportedVersions across both eras, capabilities, instructions shared with initialize so the two cannot disagree, and serverInfo under _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'], plus the ttlMs/cacheScope that CacheableResult requires. resultType is emitted only for modern requests: it is required of a 2026-07-28 server, and the spec makes the reverse safe by requiring a client that receives no resultType to read it as complete — so the risk runs one way only, towards a strict legacy client rejecting a field its schema lacks.

THE ANSWER: the premise does not hold for pact's usage. pact's entire bd surface is list, show, create, label add; only the last two mutate, and bd performs no git operations for either. Measured with unrelated work staged first: HEAD unmoved, staging untouched, no index.lock — for the direct calls and for the end-to-end case of a sibling worktree sending a message while the main worktree held a staged new file and a staged modification.

So index.lock contention and staging bleed both require bd to commit, and it does not. A doctor check would warn about a hazard that does not exist; the internal-lease dogfooding would serialise calls that never conflict, paying a lock on every message for a measurement that says zero. Not building either is the finding, not laziness.

assumed from the evidence file, and now load-bearing parts of the fix:

1. `bd create` rejects --id together with --parent outright ("cannot specify
   both --id and --parent flags") -- bd derives a reply's id from its parent,
   so a reply or fan-out recipients 2..N cannot carry the key. Only the

Fixed in 14e0a56, exactly per the recommended design's second option: the
hand-rolled O_EXCL marker file with a wall-clock staleness heuristic is
replaced entirely with a real flock(2) on a sibling guard file. This removes
both flaws structurally rather than patching either in place:

Flaw 1 (staleness heuristic unsound under contention) is gone because there
is no heuristic left at all -- flock's exclusivity is enforced by the

now never deleted at all -- confirmed during implementation that deleting

the same path lets a fresh inode start an unrelated lock series, splitting
exclusivity), which is exactly why the bead's own note that "a token check
on Drop is not sufficient by itself" turned out to generalize: the right
fix isn't a better-guarded delete, it's not deleting at all.

Implemented in commit 39f5762. audit::Summary gains by_invoked_from (event counts per invocation point) and topology_note, both rendered in the human summary and carried in --json. Events with no invoked_from are counted as 'unknown' and rendered 'predating context stamping', never as a topology — the 'no data before <date>' convention the bead required, and the state every existing log is in. SCOPE CALL, taken under the licence the bead's own design note gave ('implement the summary section first and judge --expect on whether the summary alone answers the question in practice; splitting this bead is a fine outcome'): the --check topology --expect flag was NOT built, and is filed separately as pact-ler.5 rather than dropped. Reasoning: the summary already answers the question directly, a CI assertion is one jq expression over by_invoked_from, and --expect would need to define what 'worktrees' means across a mixed run (all events? any? a majority?) — an arbitrary threshold, which is precisely the failure mode docs/audit.md already records under 'a metric that returns the same answer regardless of the behaviour it claims to measure'. The merge-commit hint the bead described was also deliberately not built as specified: a repo merging ordinary feature branches has the same commit shape, so it would fire nearly everywhere. Replaced with a signal that cannot false-positive — the repository has linked worktrees NOW, at least one event is stamped, and none names a worktree. Its blind spot (worktrees deleted after a run) is documented rather than papered over. Implemented in commit d605c50. src/watch.rs: append-only chain-hashed registry at .pact/watches.jsonl under the resolved shared root, tombstones for rm, exact and directory-prefix subscriptions (prefix decided at registration from a trailing slash or a real directory, and matched on a path boundary so src/render never matches src/renderer.rs), self-exclusion, and dedup so one agent holding overlapping subscriptions is one recipient. pact watch add/rm/ls wired in main.rs. lease acquire stamps the path's git blob id via git hash-object -w into BOTH the lock file (which release already reads) and the acquired event (which audit reads); -w matters because the protocol now says commit before release, so the working tree is clean by release time and the at-acquire blob is the only surviving fixed point. renew inherits it rather than re-stamping, or a renew would hide everything done before it. release and force-release deliver; expiry does not. Delivery runs only AFTER the lock is removed, the event written and the metric counted, and notify_release is infallible by signature, so nothing about it can fail a release or change its output contract. Failures become watch-delivery-failed events. Diffs are capped at 200 lines with a notice naming HEAD, and the blob-to-blob diff headers are relabelled with the real filename so the result reads as (and applies as) an ordinary diff. Four new event kinds, all neutral in audit::reconstruct (tested). audit summary gains watches_active/diffs_delivered/deliveries_failed. AGENTS.md block gains the two lines; docs/watch.md documents the model, the at-acquire-baseline reasoning, the cap, the worktree pre-merge caveat and the corrected motivation numbers. SCOPE NOTE: spec item 4 asked the 'message-on-contention check' to count notified deliveries as satisfying communication. No such check exists — audit has DoubleWin, StaleHolds, ChainIntegrity and CommitCorrelation — so nothing was taught; the delivery counts went into the summary instead, which is where a reader compares them against refused events.
